title: Workspace OS, organization workspaces, workspace scope, invitations
grouping: The workspace surface: the Workspace OS dashboard routes, the organization-workspace CRUD and membership routes, the shared workspace-scope resolver (no routes of its own — proven through the routers that call it), and the invitation lifecycle that admits people into those workspaces.

gaps.reason: The payload is the host machine (chip, cores, RAM, disks, GPU backends). Pinned to depth 2: the envelope and the top-level key set are the contract; the leaves are '@any'.
Same: the recommendation catalog is derived from the probe, and the tri-state family grouping depends on installed engines. Pinned to depth 2.
Reaches the plugin installer, which downloads and writes a skill directory. Only the `plugin`-less branch (which records the intent) is captured.

SKILLS_DIR is package-relative (latticeai/core/skills), not data-dir-relative, so the success branch deletes a directory inside the *installed package* — the generator will not write there. Only the not-installed branch is captured, and it is a 500 because the handler has no FileNotFoundError arm.

Needs a connected local knowledge source, which belongs to the local_files/local_knowledge families (WP R6). Only the unknown-source branch is captured — and it is a 500, because the handler has no arm for the store's ValueError.
A populated neighbourhood needs graph ingestion (WP R6). The empty-neighbourhood answer is captured.
_fetch_skills_marketplace is stubbed to a one-item canned catalog (fixture-remote/fixture-remote-skill). The live function hits GitHub and is not reproducible.

The handler sorts newest-first by wall-clock timestamp. Events that share a second change order when a slow probe ticks the clock. After capture, every `events` list is re-sorted by (event_type, area, category, payload). The Rust replay should apply the same sort before comparing.
